title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: All Objective personnel
tiers.description: Directors, executive leadership team members, senior managers, and all employees and contractors of the Objective Group. Subject to the general insider trading prohibition, avoidance of short-term trading, no procurement of others to trade, and the general prohibition on granting security over unvested Objective Securities.

tiers.name: Designated Officers
tiers.description: Directors of each Objective Group entity, the CEO, CFO, Company Secretary, Chief Legal Officer and in-house lawyers, ELT members, Key Management Personnel (as defined in the Corporations Act), and any person designated in writing by the Company Secretary. Subject to Non-Trading Periods, prior and subsequent notification requirements, the 3-month short-term dealing rule, and extra loan-security, margin loan, share lending and hedging restrictions.

definitions.hedging_definition: any transaction which operates to hedge the exposure of shares or share rights that are unvested or have yet to be issued by the plan manager under any share or option incentive plan

windows.start_anchor: 15 days prior to the last day of the half-year reporting period (31 December)
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the corresponding half-year results announcement

windows.start_anchor: 15 days prior to the last day of the full-year reporting period (30 June)
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the corresponding full-year results announcement

windows.start_anchor: 15 days before Objective's Annual General Meeting (AGM)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other period as a Non-Trading Period from time-to-time. The Policy does not address whether such additional periods are kept confidential.

rules.detail: No definition of 'Dealing' or derivative-specific rule exists; 'Securities' is defined as shares, options, debentures (including convertible notes) and other securities of Objective, with no reference to OTC derivatives or agreements to deal. An OTC put/call is not named and there is no dealing definition to sweep it in.
Hedging of unvested or unissued plan shares/rights by a Designated Officer plan participant is prohibited unless the Board gives prior written approval.
rules.evidence: A Designated Officer who is a participant under an Objective share or option incentive plan is prohibited from entering into any transaction which operates to hedge the exposure of shares or share rights that are unvested or have yet to be issued by the plan manager under any share or option incentive plan, unless prior approval is provided by the Board in writing.

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition in 3(j) is expressly limited to unvested or unissued plan securities; hedging of vested shares is not separately named and is only potentially caught by the general insider trading and short-term dealing rules.
The hedging prohibition in 3(j) applies only to Designated Officers who are plan participants; it is not extended to other Objective personnel.
No monetisation, prepaid forward, or collar structure is named, and there is no 'Dealing' definition capturing agreements to deal or derivative creation.
Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
A Designated Officer may not use Objective Securities in a share lending arrangement unless the Board gives prior written approval.
rules.evidence: in any share lending arrangement, unless prior approval is provided by the Board in writing.

rules.detail: Share lending restrictions apply only to Designated Officers; not addressed for other personnel.
CFDs are not mentioned; there is no dealing definition extending to financial products created over Securities.

All personnel are banned outright, with no approval route, from granting any form of security (including via margin loan) over Objective Securities that have yet to vest or be issued under a share or option incentive plan.
rules.evidence: prohibited, at any time, from granting, directly or indirectly, any form of security (e.g. mortgage, charge, pledge or other type of security) over any of Objective’s Securities where the shares or rights to shares have yet to vest or be issued under any share or option incentive plan offered by Objective.

rules.detail: No margin lending restriction is stated for personnel other than Designated Officers once shares have vested.

Restates the general ban: a Designated Officer may not use unvested or unissued plan shares/rights as security in any loan arrangement, including a margin loan; no approval route is given for this specific prohibition.
rules.evidence: as security in any loan arrangement where Objective’s shares or rights to shares have yet to vest or be issued to the Designated Officer under any share or option incentive plan offered by Objective

rules.detail: A Designated Officer may use vested Objective Securities in a margin loan with prior written approval from the CEO or the Board.
rules.evidence: in any margin loan, unless prior approval is provided by the CEO or Board in writing

rules.detail: Covers any mortgage, charge, pledge or other form of security over unvested/unissued plan Securities, for all personnel, at any time, with no exemption route.
rules.evidence: prohibited, at any time, from granting, directly or indirectly, any form of security (e.g. mortgage, charge, pledge or other type of security) over any of Objective’s Securities where the shares or rights to shares have yet to vest or be issued under any share or option incentive plan offered by Objective.

rules.detail: No general prohibition on granting security over vested shares outside the specific margin loan (Designated Officers only) and share lending (Designated Officers only) clauses.
Any secured financing arrangement (mortgage, charge, pledge or other security) over unvested or unissued plan Securities is banned outright for all personnel, with no exemption authority named.
rules.evidence: prohibited, at any time, from granting, directly or indirectly, any form of security (e.g. mortgage, charge, pledge or other type of security) over any of Objective’s Securities where the shares or rights to shares have yet to vest or be issued under any share or option incentive plan offered by Objective.

rules.detail: The only named secured-financing route on vested shares is a margin loan by a Designated Officer, and only with prior written CEO or Board approval; no other secured financing structure (e.g. a bank loan secured by pledge outside a 'margin loan') is separately addressed.
rules.evidence: in any margin loan, unless prior approval is provided by the CEO or Board in writing

rules.detail: For personnel who are not Designated Officers, secured financing arrangements over vested Objective Securities are not addressed.

Soft, non-binding guidance for all personnel to avoid short-term buying and selling; no defined holding period, clearance step or sanction is attached, and exercise of employee incentive scheme options is expressly excluded from 'short-term trading'.
rules.evidence: All Objective personnel ... should avoid short-term buying and selling of Objective’s Securities. Please note that transactions related to the exercise of options on Objective’s Securities under any employee incentive scheme are not considered “short-term trading” for the purposes of this prohibition.

rules.detail: Designated Officers are banned from buying and selling Objective Securities within any 3-month period unless the Board gives prior written approval.
rules.evidence: Designated Officers are not permitted to buy and sell Objective’s Securities within any 3 month period, unless approval is provided by the Board in writing.

clearance.approver: CFO and Company Secretary (or CEO if the Designated Officer is the CFO or Company Secretary)
clearance.post_trade_to: CFO and Company Secretary (or CEO if the Designated Officer is the CFO or Company Secretary)
clearance.evidence: All notifications must be in writing (this includes email) and provide Objective’s CFO and Company Secretary with at least 7 days’ notice of the proposed trade. ... Designated Officers must notify Objective’s CFO and Company Secretary ... of all trades in Objective’s Securities within 2 business days.

clearance.approver: CFO and Company Secretary (pre-screen), then CEO or the Board (Board only if the applicant is the CEO)
clearance.evidence: The Designated Officer applies to Objective’s CFO and Company Secretary for approval to trade and satisfies Objective’s CFO and Company Secretary that an exceptional circumstance has arisen and the trade is the only reasonable course of action to take ... Objective’s CEO or the Board agrees that an exceptional circumstance applies and gives prior approval for the trade in writing.

carve_outs: exercise of options on Objective's Securities under any employee incentive scheme
short_term.evidence: All Objective personnel ... should avoid short-term buying and selling of Objective’s Securities.

short_term.basis: any 3 month period, unless Board approval given
carve_outs: exercise of options on Objective's Securities under any employee incentive scheme
short_term.evidence: Designated Officers are not permitted to buy and sell Objective’s Securities within any 3 month period, unless approval is provided by the Board in writing.

exceptions.approver: CEO or Board (Board only if applicant is the CEO)
exceptions.evidence: Severe financial hardship: a pressing financial commitment or tax liability that can only be satisfied by selling the relevant Objective’s Securities.

exceptions.approver: CEO or Board (Board only if applicant is the CEO)
exceptions.evidence: Court Order: a requirement to trade in Objective’s Securities as a result of: (a) a court order; (b) court enforceable undertakings (e.g. as part of a bona fide family settlement); or (c) some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement
Other exceptional circumstances: other circumstances considered genuinely exceptional by the board.
transactions related to the exercise of options on Objective’s Securities under any employee incentive scheme are not considered “short-term trading” for the purposes of this prohibition.

exemption_authority: The CEO or the Board (Board alone if the applicant is the CEO), after CFO/Company Secretary pre-screening, may approve trading in a Non-Trading Period, or otherwise-prohibited dealing, on hardship, court order or other genuinely exceptional grounds (para 4). The Board alone may approve the 3(j) hedging prohibition, the 3(i)(iii) share lending prohibition and the 3(g) short-term dealing rule; the CEO or Board may approve the 3(i)(ii) margin loan restriction. No exemption route exists for the unvested-securities loan-security ban in 3(h)/3(i)(i).

bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited, at any time, from granting, directly or indirectly, any form of security ... over any of Objective’s Securities where the shares or rights to shares have yet to vest or be issued
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a collar can never be secured on unvested shares or rights, for anyone, and there is no exemption authority for this specific ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in any margin loan, unless prior approval is provided by the CEO or Board in writing
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank's secured loan is structured as a margin loan over vested shares, a Designated Officer can proceed with prior written CEO or Board approval – the only named route to secured financing on vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Officers are not permitted to use any of Objective’s Securities as follows: ... (ii) in any margin loan ... (iii) in any share lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Margin loan and share lending restrictions target only Designated Officers; for other vested-share holders, secured financing on vested shares is not addressed at all, though the general insider trading and (non-binding) short-term trading guidance still apply.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging scope limited to unvested plan shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited from entering into any transaction which operates to hedge the exposure of shares or share rights that are unvested or have yet to be issued
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The derivative legs of a collar over vested shares fall outside the named hedging prohibition entirely; they are only potentially caught, if at all, by the undefined general insider trading and short-term dealing rules.

bespoke_clauses.topic: notification not preclearance for ordinary trades
bespoke_clauses.clause: The person who receives the notice of intention to buy or sell shares, is not authorised to prevent a Designated Officer from trading, but will provide guidance
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside Non-Trading Periods, a Designated Officer need only give 7 days' prior written notice (not obtain approval) before dealing, and cannot be blocked, so entering collar derivatives faces a low procedural bar once outside a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: everyone at Objective is expected to demonstrate integrity when dealing with shares, options, debentures (including convertible notes) and other securities (collectively, Securities)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because the Policy never defines 'Dealing' or 'trade' to expressly capture derivative creation or agreements to deal, an OTC put/call over Objective shares arguably sits outside the Policy's operative provisions except via the general insider-trading prohibition, creating interpretive uncertainty for a bank counterparty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (no provision addressing a financier's or lender's forced sale during a Non-Trading Period)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, there is no express breach trigger if a lender enforces security and sells during a blackout, leaving that risk entirely unaddressed rather than expressly prohibited.

summary: A funded collar over vested shares is workable for a Designated Officer if the bank's loan is structured as a margin loan, since 3(i)(ii) permits margin loans over vested Objective Securities with prior written approval from the CEO or the Board; the hedging prohibition (3(j)) and the loan-security bans (3(h), 3(i)(i)) apply only to unvested or unissued plan securities and do not reach vested shares. The put and call legs are not expressly regulated as derivatives or dealings – the Policy has no defined 'Dealing' term extending to OTC derivatives or agreements to deal – so they are governed only by the general insider trading prohibition and the non-binding short-term trading guidance (a binding 3-month buy/sell restriction applies only to Designated Officers, again waivable by the Board). Execution, unwind or delivery must sit outside the half-year, full-year and AGM Non-Trading Periods (or obtain exceptional-circumstances approval from the CEO/Board) and the officer must not hold inside information. For personnel who are not Designated Officers, financing of vested shares is not addressed by the Policy at all, so a funded collar for that group faces no policy-specific bar beyond the general insider trading law. Overall, the structure is achievable subject to CEO/Board approval of the loan as a margin loan, timing around blackout periods, and the unresolved question of whether the undefined 'dealing' concept catches the OTC derivative legs.
